To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the results obtained from our calculations of the unsteady transonic flows over an oscillating airfoil are in good agreement with the available experimental data.
the unsteady flow over a pitching airfoil is highly nonlinear, and that the viscous flow is more nonlinear than inviscid flow.
the shock-wave motion is not a simple function of reduced frequency and the shock-wave motion can be significantly affected by viscous effects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of the unsteady transonic flow around an airfoil.
the development and validation of a computer code for calculating unsteady, transonic flows over oscillating airfoils.
the development and validation of a numerical method for the solution of unsteady flow problems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the unsteady transonic flow over airfoils is a very complicated and complex phenomenon and, in general, cannot be predicted accurately without considering the effects of viscous-inviscid interactions.
, in the case of transonic flows, unsteady viscous-flow computations are required to provide accurate results.
, in general, the results of computations for unsteady transonic flows over an airfoil are in good agreement with the experimental results, but the results of computations of viscous flow are better.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the unsteady viscous-flow effects are important in the shock-wave region of the airfoil, but the unsteady inviscid-flow effects are important for the whole oscillation cycle of the airfoil.
, for this particular case, the unsteady viscous-flow calculations are superior to those for the inviscid-flow case.
we are now in a position to predict the nonlinear unsteady flow phenomena over airfoils with reasonable accuracy and with the use of reasonable computational resources.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the transonic flow regime, viscous effects should be taken into account in unsteady flow calculations, even if the Reynolds number is high.
, when the shock wave moves over the airfoil surface, the viscous effect is more pronounced than the inviscid one.
the shock motion is not as strong as that predicted by the Euler equations.
